utterances.text: This article of the law demonstrates that the object of protection and all the activities of the Army of Serbian Krajina is the territory of the Republic of Serbian Krajina. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now I'm going to read Article 3 in the same law. It's on the same page in the upper right corner in B/C/S: "Command in" -- Article 3: "Command in the army is based on the principles of the unity of command in terms of the engagement of forces and resources, single command, and the duty to execute decisions, orders, and commands of the superior commanding officer." The next paragraph: "The army is the under the command by the president of the republic pursuant to the RSK constitutions and decisions of the Supreme Defence Council." Mr. Orlic, I assume that this Article 3 - which is a universal one affecting all armies, in my opinion - says clearly that we have a single chain of command in the Army of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Simply as page 47, lines 11 to 12, I'm not necessarily disagreeing with what Mr. Lukic just said, but I would just simply ask that counsel refrain from giving his opinion and we stick to the evidence being led from the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I accept the remark by my learned friend, and I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orlic, what it says in Article 5, does that represent the essential principles of the functioning -- Article 3, excuse me, the essential principles of the functioning of the Serbian Army of the Republic of the Srpska Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The Republika Srpska at the time was formed as a state, and it had all the attributes of statehood. It had its own army, its own judicial system, all the things that a state has. So these articles would apply just like in any other country to everything that applies to the armed forces of any other country.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What does the principle of single command stand for, unity of command?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Unity of command stands for the idea that the order by a superior officer must be executed, and here what we have is command by the command --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one moment, please. We have an objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, my concern is that this witness has been called as a fact witness. I will withdraw my objection at this time. Well -- I will withdraw my objection at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you going to reinstate it at some other time?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Hopefully not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Hopefully not. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not going to go into much theory with the witness, but I just wanted to clarify certain facts which are important for me in this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This means that the person who is in the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina has one superior in that army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And the supreme commander of that army, the highest in authority is the president of the Republic of Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. At the time it was President Martic, at that time. He was the commander-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And there is nobody above him in this chain of command in this army.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No. He has his own counsel for defence, and there is the commander of the Army of the Republic of Serbian Krajina who executes all the orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: All right. That army commander and his superior -- is his subordinate; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: When you were there for the second time briefly, and as you said you were not assigned any duties, you were part of the Serbian Krajina army; is that correct? But you were not assigned to any particular duty nor were you given any kind of establishment rank in that army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, but I was sent there. I went there, I was there, but I did not have any establishment post or position.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Judge Moloto asked you during the examination-in-chief if you had received any order to go back to the Army of Yugoslavia, and what I understood was that you had talked to the commander, Commander Novakovic, and that he allowed you or gave his permission for you to return to Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Because of illness, I was sent for home treatment by the military hospital in Knin. I was sent to Belgrade, but still I had to have permission from Commander Novakovic to do this because I did not have another superior. I was not deployed or assigned anywhere, so he was the only person that I could ask for this permission from.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you told him that after treatment you wanted to go back to the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No, we didn't discuss that. All he did was permit me to return to Belgrade, and he did not order me to come back to the Krajina again.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking you. He did not order you to return to the Krajina and to serve again in the Serbian Army of the Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He didn't order me to do that, and that is why I reported to the command of the 1st Army.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Neither did he in any way ask you when you came to the 1st Army -- when you returned to the Army of Yugoslavia from the hospital, that is, to go to the Serbian army in the Krajina. He didn't ask you to do that, did he?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No, nobody asked me to go back there, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He didn't issue an order to that effect nor was he against you going to the Army of Yugoslavia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. He wasn't opposed to me going back to the Army of Yugoslavia nor did he order me to return to the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're talking about his oral permission for you to go to Yugoslavia for treatment; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The same as when you testified on page 28, line 9, today, that when you received oral permission from your superior in the Army of Yugoslavia to go for a talk with Celeketic and then to go again to the Army of Srpska Krajina, that, again, was an oral order, was it not?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, we are going to your third stay in the Serbian Army of the Krajina and service. When you -- let's clarify this. When you became the chief of the security organ of the Main Staff of the Serbian Army of the Krajina, you served from then on in the Serbian Army of the Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: One correction: The chief of the intelligence department. And when I assumed my duties there, I was serving in the Army of the Republic of Srpska Krajina until I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That is correct. So this duty and the deployment to the establishment post that you referred to just now was something that was given to you by the superior officer in the Army of Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. When I was posted as the chief of the intelligence department of the Serbian Army of the Krajina by the Krajina command, that's how it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we look at document 1D00-9116 on the e-court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop before we do that. What do you want to do with 6367?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to have that document -- actually, I deliberately mentioned the first few articles. The law is quite detailed, and I would just like to have this first page of the Law of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Krajina admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The first page of 6367 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D85.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Now, what document did you want on the screen, Mr. Lukic, now, after that one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, it is 1D00-9116 in the e-court. And for the court officer in Belgrade, the document is marked ERN 0611-4939. This is again a document that's part of the personnel dossier, but I don't know if it's been admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orlic, the heading of this document says "order number ... assistant to the commander for security-intelligence." Can you please look at the signature. Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: The document was signed by the assistant commander for security intelligence tasks, Colonel Dusan Smiljanic, and if I may comment?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you do that anyway, but can you please answer one more question before that. Is this a document that was issued by the Serbian Army of the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is a document issued by the Serbian Army of the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In this document, you are being appointed to the Main Staff of the Serbian Army of the Krajina in the security intelligence sector to the duty of chief of the intelligence department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now go ahead. You wanted to say something. This was important to me, but if you have a comment, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say something about this document. This was an attempt of a sort and a reflection of an intention to form a sector or department for intelligence and security which encompassed both security and intelligence assignments. However, this never actually was implemented, and Colonel Smiljanic was not my superior, even though he did sign this document. These two departments actually were separate throughout that whole period, and my superior was General Loncar who was the chief of the command staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: From what I understand, in that army the intelligence organ has the same, let's say, level as the security organ, and they are both subordinated to the Chief of Staff; is that correct or not?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: The security organ is subordinated to the commander, and the intelligence organ is subordinated to the Chief of Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. In any case, do you agree with me that from the time you were appointed to this post in the Serbian Army of the Krajina, perhaps even before that, but in any case, from that point on you were in the command -- chain of command of the Serbian Army of the Krajina in the Main Staff, or under the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. From the time I came and assumed this duty until I left, I was within the chain of command of the Army of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And you had nothing to do with the chain of command from the Army of Yugoslavia from that point onwards.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No connection and no duties arising from that did I have in relation to the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Pursuant to Article 3 of the Law of the Army of the Serbian Republic of the Srpska Krajina, all orders, commands, and information and reports were sent to your superior in that army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: All the orders were received in the Army of the Republic of Srpska Krajina from them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And among these orders, return reports were sent to your superiors in that army; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic, maybe you might clarify this with the witness. I'm not quite sure at line 9, page 54, line 10, who that "them" are: "All the orders were received in the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina from them."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orlic, you heard. I just want us to be quite precise. When you replied, you said: "All orders are received in the Army of the Serbian Krajina from them." When you say "from them," who did you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Yes, all the orders were received from the command of the Army of the Republic of the Serbian Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document for admission, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D86.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the examination-in-chief, you explained that throughout the whole time that you were in the Serbian Army of the Krajina, you received your salary in Yugoslavia from the Army of Yugoslavia through the accounting centre. And what I am saying is that it is the accounting centre of the Ministry of Defence. Do you remember anything about that? Do you recall who issued your salary payments, or perhaps you don't remember.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: During the SFRY, the accounting centre was under the Secretariat for National Defence. They would be issuing the allocated salaries for the Army of Yugoslavia, the Territorial Defence for the retired personnel. And I assume that that's what was going on when the Army of Yugoslavia was formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: But you were also receiving some sort of supplement from the Serbian Army of Srpska Krajina or from the authorities there. Can you please tell us what that was?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: The Serbian Republic of Krajina had its own money. They were printing its own money, and so they paid all members of the Army of the Republika Srpska Krajina who were there permanently and were part of that army. Those of us who -- for example, I, who was there, I was receiving a supplement to cover the cost of my expenses in the Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I assume, then, that the money that was at your -- on your account in Belgrade that you were receiving as a salary in Yugoslavia was meant for the expenses of your family. Is that what they were using if you didn't need this money while you were in the Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct. They had to have some means of livelihood.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We have already heard a lot of evidence here relating to the period of hyperinflation and the economic situation in that time. Do you recall that during 1993 and 1994 if this salary that your family was receiving in Yugoslavia was something that was important for the livelihood of your family in view of the hyperinflation and the general worthlessness of the money?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Well, if my wife managed to take out the salary on the same day that it was deposited on the account, she could perhaps have a counter-value of German marks. If she withdrew this money the following day, then the amount would be less, and it was very difficult to live on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, perhaps we could take our break now. I don't have too many questions. I just wanted to inform you, but I just wanted to actually go through my questions at the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We'll take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I proceed, Your Honours, I have a slight correction on page 56, line 15. The witness said, when I asked him about the salary, he said 10 German marks. Now it's correct, 10.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orlic, can you still hear me? Can we proceed?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In answering to my learned friend's questions, you answered about the intelligence jobs you did in the Serbian Army of Krajina, and I'll proceed along these lines. Your superior, as you said, was the Chief of Staff, Colonel, later on General, Loncar; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your subordinate in the command chain was Lieutenant-Colonel Knezevic; am I right. I'm not sure about his rank, though.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, he was lieutenant-colonel.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, but was he subordinate? The witness is subordinate?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's how I understood that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: What was the duty of Lieutenant-Colonel Knezevic? What did he do? What was his job?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Lieutenant-Colonel Knezevic was the chief of the intelligence centre, which was subordinated to me personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Very well. On your examination-in-chief and at the beginning of cross-examination, you spoke about the duties of an intelligence organ. I'm interested in the exchange of information that you had with the intelligence organs of the Army of Yugoslavia and the intelligence organs of the Army of Republika Srpska. The information in question is -- the information that was exchanged among the three armies, it was about the communication between the three armies; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For example, when you needed information from a certain army, you could receive such an order, an order to that effect only from your superior Loncar in the form of an order.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No, no. This was my obligation as an intelligence organ. In case I did not have enough indicia or indicators for any activities that was happening on the part of the other armies, I had to request from the intelligence organ of the Army of Republika Srpska or the intelligence administration of the General Staff the missing information through my direct communication with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: However, that was still within the function that you had the Army of the Republic of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was my function.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you communicate with them directly or in some other form? What was your communication like? Did you --

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: We communicated by way of telegrams.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Did you ever communicate with anybody from the intelligence administration personally, orally, by phone?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No, never. We never spoke by phone. None of them ever came to Knin or to the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: My learned friend Saxon asked you about General Celeketic, what his status was; that was on page 24. You answered that according to what you know, he had joined from the Army of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would now like the witness to be shown 65 ter 6126.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I see the document, may I provide a somewhat more detailed explanation or answer? Before becoming the commander of the Army of Republika of Serbian Krajina, I believe that he was in Western Slavonia, also a member of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina. I believe that that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I understood you. I don't know whether you've seen the document before. Take a moment to look at it.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: This document applies to Dusan Loncar; right?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, you're right. I apologise. But still, we can have a look at the document. Dusan Loncar, who is the Chief of Staff in the Main Staff of the Serbian Army of Krajina, this was during the period when you were still there; right? Do you know that he was promoted by Milan Martic and that he received the rank of general and that decision was made by the president of the Republic of Serbian Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I know that. I know that he was a general of the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the document please be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, that becomes Exhibit D87.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, can the witness please be shown P171 -- or rather, 00171. This is the document referring to Celeketic that I originally had in mind.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you've seen this document before. Again, before you were appointed and left and joined the Serbian Vojina of Krajina in 1994, do you know that General Celeketic was appointed the commander of the Serbian Army of Krajina by the president of the Serbian Republic of Krajina?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We no longer need that document, and can I now please show the witness 1D00-9160, for the court officer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What do you want to do with this one?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You called it 00171. You started off with saying P171, then you said 00171. Now, I don't know whether it's -- is it a P or is it --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I apologise. It was a P document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Of course. I'm going to repeat the number, but I am afraid that the court officer in Belgrade will not be able to find the document under that number because we just introduced it. The number is 1D00-9160. The -- and for the court officer in Belgrade, it is an order number 5/6-127 for Dusan Smiljanic, dated 26 May 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Witness, do you have the document in front of you, the one that I've just cited?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: About Mr. Smiljanic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct. That's the Dusan Smiljanic who signed your decision when you were given a duty in the Serbian Army of Krajina; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And it arises from this document that on the 26th of May, 1994, he was appointed the assistant commander for security and intelligence of the Serbian Army of Krajina; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And that decision on his appointment was signed by General Celeketic?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we have -- can we please have this document admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D88, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Orlic, earlier today you described the way you submitted your request to be pensioned off, and you said who you've submitted it to. On page 36 of today's transcript, you said that before you submitted your written request that the Prosecutor showed you, that you had addressed your superiors in the Serbian Army of Krajina and asked for their consent to be pensioned off or, rather, to submit your request for retirement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe that it was either Loncar or Celeketic.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: To General Loncar who was my superior.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: He agreed; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Not immediately. It took persuading. We spent a somewhat longer time talking about my return, and finally he agreed because I'd explained the reasons for which I had to leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In any case, you did not submit any requests before you were given his approval; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the Court please produce P734; page 10 in B/C/S, page 7 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether you are aware of this document. This is an instruction issued by General Perisic. I'm going to read Article 34 very slowly, and this article concerns the return transfer of professional soldiers and civilian personnel from command centres. And Article 34 says -- I don't know if you have the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it slowly. "Professional soldiers and civilian personnel in the KC records whose professional military service ceases on any legal grounds shall be sent to the KC personnel department to resolve the cessation in service and for removal from the KC records with the consent and on the recommendation of the KC Main Staff." At the time, you met all the requirements for retirement; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: For early retirement under the law. However, I'm not familiar with this document at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I just want to hear from you that at the time you already met legal requirements to submit a request for early retirement; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: At the moment when you met the conditions, you first talked to your superior in the staff asking for his consent, and after some discussion he agreed.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, and then I drafted my request and handed it to the personnel department in the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: And just one more question in order to clarify some things, and I will bring my cross-examination to an end. As far as I could understand you, Mr. Orlic, all the three times when you went to Republika Srpska Krajina, the first time to join the Territorial Defence and the second and third time to the Army of Republika Srpska Krajina, you actually wanted to go there; you never objected to your going there; right?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. Every time, I wanted to go there because I hailed from the area and I wanted to go back.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's how I understood it. You said it to the Prosecutor that you were born in Korenica or in the region, and you actually wanted to go to defend your homeland and the area where your roots were.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's where I was born. That's where I completed my education. That's where I went every year.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You were personally affected by the fact that the territory where you were born, where you resided, where your roots are, came under threat and was struck by war waged by another state, and to be more precise, that it came under threat from Croatia?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, you are right. I wanted to help in one way or another. I wanted to help the people there, as a professional.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In light of what I asked you a little while ago about salaries when you you mentioned the hyperinflation, I would suggest that money was not your primary motive. You would have gone anyway whether you were paid or not.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. In any case, I would have gone there.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no more questions for this witness, Your Honours. Thank you very much, Mr. Orlic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any re-examination, Mr. Saxon?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: A bit, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we please show the witness what is Exhibit P1047.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Mr. Orlic, during cross-examination my colleague at page 58 asked you about the exchange of information that you did with the Army of Republika Srpska and the Army of Yugoslavia. I have a document that I'd like to show you, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And first of all, if we can turn to the last page, and in English this would be document ID 0620-0218.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you see, Mr. Orlic, at the upper left-hand side we see the words "Chief of the Intelligence Department, Colonel Rade Orlic," here on this last page of the document. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Is this -- and then down below, it's not so easy to read, but there appears to be kind of a stamp. Was this a telegram?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the first page, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But I can --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Orlic. I cut you off. Can you repeat what you just said?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes, the stamp I can see, but I can't see who this is from.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we go to the first page, please, in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: This is the first page of the document, Mr. Orlic. And looking at the heading, that it's from the republic of the Serbian Krajina Main Staff of the Serbian Army. It's titled: "Weekly information for the period of 4 September 1994 to 11 September 1994." I'm wondering whether you can recognise this document.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the document, but I can see my name on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. Was this the kind of document that -- or the kind of telegram that you would have written during your exchange of information, a document like this?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: No. Those were purely -- you mean later? Those were purely documents about activities and the movements of the troops of the neighbouring armies that I was monitoring. It's a kind of broader document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: I guess my question is, did you have occasion to write broader documents such as this one?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember writing broader documents. The documents that I drafted were usually short, one page long at the most.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: All right. We can leave this document for now. Can we see what was Exhibit P171 again, please. This was I believe shown by my learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: And you see, I believe this is the appointment of General Loncar to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Excuse me, I have the wrong document. This is the appointment of General Celeketic. I'm wondering if my learned friend can help me with the exhibit number -- D87, please. If we could see D87.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: We see this document, the promotional document of General Loncar. It's dated 16 December 1994. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADE ORLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we see now Exhibit P409, please. Court's indulgence, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Can we move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Orlic, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you so much for taking the time off to come and testify at the Tribunal. You are now excused. You may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank the Trial Chamber for allowing me to testify in this manner in view of my health condition.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We appreciate you are coming, we appreciate the effort. It's appreciated. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Saxon.

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not have another witness available today. Our next witness is available on Tuesday, the 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The 5th? Tuesday?

utterances.speaker: MR. SAXON
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then, the Chamber stands adjourned to Tuesday, the 5th of May, at 9.00 in the morning, Courtroom I. Court adjourned.
